name: xaviersobased
label: Atlantic
lede: A Manhattan kid who traded a gaming headset for a microphone, uploaded 'patchmade' to the internet, and ended up with a major-label debut that Pitchfork scored 8.3.

eras.title: A kid on the Upper West Side
eras.text: Xavier Lopez grew up in a Manhattan family that had lived on the Upper West Side for four decades, with a DJ mother and a DJ brother. The internet did the rest of the teaching.

years.src: Wikipedia: Xaviersobased · The FADER: Cover Story
years.h: Age ten, YouTube serves him Yung Lean's 'Hurt'
years.p: The autoplay rabbit hole runs through Lil B, Bladee and Black Kray. Lopez has since credited Chief Keef, Hi-C and Duwap Kaine too.
years.xp: Lopez was born October 23, 2003, on the Upper West Side. His older brother, who DJs as Nurse, had already handed him skateboarding, Odd Future and A$AP Rocky. Yung Lean's 2013 single 'Hurt' was the first step down the cloud-rap and digicore hole.

q: It means effortless swag and positivity.
years.src: The FADER: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Xaviersobased
years.h: First beat on SoundCloud, name lifted from an old iCloud account
years.p: He starts producing at twelve on an FL Studio demo. The stage name nods to Lil B's idea of being based.
years.xp: Lopez told The FADER that 'based' means 'effortless swag and positivity'. He joined the online rap collectives [[Novagang|ed733f70-2be1-4352-aa3f-f12b770653fa]] and Jewelxxet in these years, releasing tapes and EPs on SoundCloud.

eras.title: Gaming clan, music crew
eras.text: Lockdown turns a Tony Hawk's Underground Pro friend group into the collective that names a genre.

years.src: The FADER: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Xaviersobased
years.h: He swaps a gaming headset for a mic and starts 1c34
years.p: The collective begins as a gaming clan during COVID lockdowns, with friends including [[Ksuuvi|25f406de-7368-49f0-b4ef-eb64ffbc0b61]] and Backend.
years.xp: According to The FADER, 1c34 'began as a gaming clan' before it became a music crew. Wikipedia credits the group with pioneering the jerk microgenre of the 2020s. Wikipedia's collective overview dates 1c34 to 2021, while Lopez's biography dates the formation to 2020.

eras.title: The patchmade year
eras.text: One song catches on without the algorithm's help, and a New York scene grows around it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Xaviersobased · The FADER: Cover Story
years.p: Produced by Kashpaint, it is the track The Face called a jerk anthem and Rolling Stone called a passing headrush.
years.xp: Lopez says he never chased the algorithm: 'I never really played into it... That's why it grew how it grew.' DJ Rennessy first saw him play at an East River park show in summer 2022 and spotted the potential right away.

years.src: The FADER: Novagang · The FADER: Song You Need
years.h: [[Novagang|ed733f70-2be1-4352-aa3f-f12b770653fa]] drops H.T.N.G. Vol 2 and sells out a New York show
years.p: The compilation lands two weeks before a sold-out NYC show headlined by [[osquinn|46a0eeec-1137-4303-85eb-ad11addbe5e4]] and xaviersobased.
years.xp: The FADER describes Novagang as an outsider crew that rejects the label hyperpop, with xaviersobased and osquinn among its central acts. A month later the site picked his track 'fuck the city up' from Stash Muzik as a Song You Need.

eras.title: Keep it goin
eras.text: Two mixtapes, one leak, and a Pitchfork audience for a SoundCloud regular.

years.h: '40' with [[Nettspend|4585749c-5489-4699-9daf-1ffa9717179f]] and [[Evilgiane|18cf137c-6d0f-4e9b-ab9a-a2cc96283ad9]], then an On the Radar freestyle
years.p: '40' came out January 11. The next day he freestyled for the online show On the Radar, which was later released as 'Special'.

years.src: Pitchfork: Keep It Goin Xav · Wikipedia: Xaviersobased
years.h: Keep It Goin Xav: 15 tracks, hosted by [[DJ Rennessy|ed000c84-a712-47e7-a14c-2de888c6e3be]]
years.p: Guests include Nettspend, Yhapojj, Jtxpo and Kuru. Pitchfork's Alphonse Pierre called it vibrant, improvisatory and fun as hell.
years.xp: Pierre wrote that Xaviersobased keeps a strong New York rap identity despite his amorphous influences. It was a SoundCloud-exclusive release.

years.big: "It's sweet to watch someone who doesn't give a fuck."
years.h: With 2 leaks, so he ships it half-finished
years.p: Wikipedia reports the tape leaked a week earlier and went out unfinished. That is Kieran Press-Reynolds in Pitchfork.
years.xp: The album line is quoted as printed in Pitchfork's review of With 2. Some sources give the release only as June 2024; Wikipedia gives June 5.

eras.title: Osamason, shoegaze, Atlantic
eras.text: He co-writes a rage-meets-jerk EP, adds guitars, and signs to a major.

years.p: 'whole lotta' and 'Shitshow' are new; 'Shitshow' is produced by ok. Hosted by DJ Rennessy.
years.xp: The FADER framed it as mutual respect: OsamaSon had paid homage to Xaviersobased on the site's Would You Rather? series, and the pair had teamed up for a year or so already.

years.src: The Face: Xaviersobased and Osamason · Wikipedia: Xaviersobased · Pitchfork: Once More
years.h: Once More EP puts him in front of a wall of shoegaze guitars
years.p: The Face heard him and OsamaSon on 'Uncomfy' outrunning a mushy shoegaze backdrop. It is his first release as an Atlantic signee.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Atlantic signing to 2025 without a month. The Face called him one of the most compelling experimentalists in contemporary rap, even as he described the EP as a warm-up for album mode.

eras.title: Xavier
eras.text: A debut album under his own name, on Surf Gang, 1-chance and Atlantic.

years.src: Wikipedia: Xavier · NME: Xaviersobased · The FADER: Cover Story
years.p: Pitchfork scored it 8.3. Lead single 'iPhone 16' came out January 23.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists features from Skrillex, OsamaSon, Zaytoven, Rio da Yung OG and Dylan Brady, and production from Eddiepoz, Ss3bby, [[Ksuuvi|25f406de-7368-49f0-b4ef-eb64ffbc0b61]] and Yung Sherman. NME picked out 'Clorox' and 'Heartfelt'. The FADER released a documentary, Keep It Goin', on February 13.

years.h: Riverside 2.0 tour, then Ken Carson's Xperimenting run
years.p: U.S. and European dates in March and April, then 14 U.S. shows opening for Ken Carson from August 26 to September 23.
